She has always been fascinated by elephants and her mission is to investigate why these beautiful animals are in such danger. The Indian elephant is classified as endangered, and Malaika learns that the biggest threats they face are forest fragmentation and living in captivity. She goes undercover to find out more about elephants in the tourist trade in Indian cities and then visits an elephant hospital run by Wildlife SOS, a charity which rehabilitates elephants rescued from captivity. Some of the elephants here were in chains for over 50 years and now have a chance to enjoy life in the wild. channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Oral Histories
channel.desc: C-SPAN's American History TV is remembers September 11, 2001, through the stories of Americans who were at the White House, the Capitol, the Pentagon - and in the skies above Washington.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: 9/11 Twenty Five Years
channel.desc: C-SPAN tours the permanent outdoor memorial to the 184 people who were killed in the Pentagon and on American Airlines Flight 77 during the September 11, 2001, attacks.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: The Day and the Decade
channel.desc: Current and former news anchors for ABC, CBS, CNN and FOX talk about their coverage of the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, and the years since. Marvin Kalb moderates the program.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Oral Histories
channel.desc: Mary Beth Cahill talks about the events of Sept. 11, 2001, when she was Sen. Edward Kennedy's chief of staff.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Father and Daughter Pilots Reflect on September 11, 2001
channel.desc: As one of the first DC Air National Guard F-16 pilots scrambled from Andrews Air Force Base on Sept. 11, 2001, Heather Penney talks about her experiences that day.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Tom McMillan, Flight 93
channel.desc: Author Tom McMillan discusses his book, Flight 93 - The Story, the Aftermath, and the Legacy of American Courage on 9/11. United Flight 93 crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, on September 11, 2001.

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: 9/11 Twenty Five Years

channel.name: CSPAN 2 US
channel.title: Q & A

channel.title: Max & Samuel Holleran, Scattered Steel - The Afterlife of the World Trade Center
channel.desc: Authors Max & Samuel Holleran (Scattered Steel) trace the journey of the World Trade Center's remains after the September 11, 2001 attacks.[(96057)]

channel.desc: Laura Ingraham is one of the most listened to women on political talk radio in the country. Ingraham earned a B.A. degree at Dartmouth college and a Juris Doctor degree at the University of Virginia School of Law. She took the knowledge from her J.D. degree and applied it to serve as a litigator and Supreme Court law clerk. She is also the best-selling author of five books. Tune in to watch"The Ingraham Angle," as the program serves to discuss the issues that are being overlooked and other issues that are causing turmoil in the United States.
